# Seed review pack — s 43 examples, for correction

> **Nothing in this document is approved, and none of it is project
> content.** Every record below was written by a machine to show what a
> Stage 0 record *looks like* when it is filled in over the pilot area.
> The legal judgements in it are unverified and some of them are wrong.
> That is the design: it is easier to correct a wrong answer than to
> compose a right one from an empty form, and your corrections are what
> becomes the real gold set (ADR-0043).

> **What to do with it.** Read a record, read the passage under it, and
> say one of three things: *correct*, *amend* (and say how), or *reject*
> (and say why). A rejection is as useful as a correction — it tells us
> the shape was wrong, not just the wording. You do not have to finish.

> **This is a scoped round: 10 records of
> 178.** They were chosen because each one is holding other
> records out of the gold set — `data/derived/reports/blockers.md`
> says which, and what each decision releases. The rest of the queue
> is unchanged and is in `data/derived/seed-review-pack.md`.

## How a record is laid out

Each one carries a **seed id** (`SEED-…`) — quote that when you write
a correction, because the record's own id may change and the seed id
will not. **Why this example** says what the record is here to
demonstrate; if the record is wrong but the point is right, amend it.
Where a record rests on a passage, the passage is quoted underneath
with the exact span in **bold**.

## Competency questions (2) — guide §5.1

### `SEED-CQ-0013` → `CQ-0013`

**Why this example.** The currency category exists because a retrieval-only system fails it silently. This one is grounded in a real trap inside the pilot: TMM/Part29/3/3/1~2 cites section 114 of the *Trade Marks Act 1905*, and that instrument is not held anywhere in the programme (Q-24), so the citation resolves to nothing at all.

| field | value |
|---|---|
| `question` | Which of the tests quoted in the section 43 material were decided under earlier legislation, and does that limit how they are used now? |
| `asked_by` | examiner |
| `category` | currency |
| `pilot_in_scope` | true |
| `expected_sources` | required: TMM/Part29/3/3/1~2; supporting: TMM/Part29/3/3/1~1 |
| `expected_concepts` | reasonable doubt; superseded legislation |
| `must_not_include` | — |
| `answer_shape` | Must name the earlier instrument explicitly, must not present the quoted passage as authority on the current section without that qualification, and must reproduce the Manual's own statement of how far the principles carry across. |
| `caveats` | The 1905 Act is not in the corpus, so the system can name the citation and can never verify or display it. |
| `measured_by` | currency; citation_correctness; authority_weighting |
